title: Quad vows to ensure open maritime corridors
summary: Leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the United States criticized what they described as “destabilizing or unilateral actions” affecting regional peace and stability, in a meeting held…

blocks.text: At the Quad summit held in Manila, Philippines on the 17th, from left to right: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, U.S. President Donald Trump, and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese pose for a commemorative photo.

MANILA, Philippines — Leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the United States criticized what they described as “destabilizing or unilateral actions” affecting regional peace and stability, in a meeting held on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Manila.
US President Donald Trump arrived yesterday and met with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae.
The countries, constituting the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad), said their group is “a force for good and a partnership of action, committed to peace, stability and prosperity.”

“We strongly oppose any destabilizing or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion, which escalate tensions and undermine regional peace and stability. We express grave concerns about economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions,” they said in a joint statement.
“We commit to work together to ensure open, safe and resilient maritime transit corridors in the Indo-Pacific.”

Quad also vowed to secure critical supply chains, protect freedom of navigation and overflight, drive growth through technologies of the future, including investments and deployment of trusted artificial intelligence (AI), and respond to disasters with life-saving assistance.

“We commit to work together to ensure open, safe and resilient maritime transit corridors in the Indo-Pacific. We are working with regional partners to tackle shared challenges and drive opportunities to deliver tangible benefits to the Indo-Pacific,” the group said.

The Quad meeting took place days before Trump’s trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China on the sidelines of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation meet.

China, whose aggressive actions in the resource-rich South China Sea has drawn widespread condemnation, had accused Quad of trying to sow enmity between Beijing and its neighbors and disrupting regional peace.

In the same statement, the four leaders also announced the inaugural Quad Business Leaders’ Forum to be held next year. The event aims to bring together business leaders, government officials and policy experts from Quad countries to foster greater business ties across private sectors.
The Quad leaders also affirmed the importance of the AI Accelerator, announced by their foreign ministers in Atlanta.
“The Accelerator is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted AI access, deployment and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific,” they said.
The group also welcomed the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration, a new initiative that seeks to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness.
It also acknowledged the “rapid increase” in the number and scale of cyber incidents in the region and announced an enhanced Quad Cybersecurity Cooperation to achieve an open and secure cyberspace.

“We unequivocally condemn terrorism and violent extremism in all its forms and manifestations, including cross-border terrorism, and commit to strengthening the Quad’s ongoing cooperation on counterterrorism,” Quad added.
The four countries also reaffirmed their “unwavering” support for ASEAN centrality and unity and committed to uphold a free and open Indo-Pacific.
